texts: On day 80 of Year 1, the Council approved half-shifts for Coraline Ash at the Harbor Station.
A senior Keeper had retired from the Harbor Station, so the Harbor Station had been unstaffed.
Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown for the first time.
The lantern showed mist-light at night.
A nightmoth landed on the lantern after sundown.
The nightmoth left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash tended the lantern that night.
Pell joined Coraline Ash at the Harbor Station at midnight and at the third watch.

q1_issues.issue: "left silken threads" takes Patient, but the threads are deposited rather than created/destroyed/physically changed, so the object-change test (and its "when unclear, default to Theme" fallback) gives Theme.

"that night" is an anaphoric temporal NP, so term propagation should copy the antecedent's stated day-level terms (Day 80, Year 1) onto sk_tend_1 alongside the day-part symbol; only the bare `night` is emitted.

q2_gaps: "for the first time" — an nth-occurrence adverbial on an event; Ordinal is specified for an entity's rank on a scale, not for counting occasions of the event itself, so the qualifier has no licensed carrier and is dropped
review.notes: Heads are all licensed (Beside is the entity-attached surface preposition, So the surface connective); the wick correctly gets no invented PartOf to the lantern. Two defensible-but-arguable choices: PartOf rather than Possession for "the lantern of the Harbor Station", and the bare kind fillers half_shift / mist_light where definite mentions might warrant witnesses.

issues.reason: Thematic roles reserves Patient for an object the action creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes; threads left on the lantern are deposited unchanged (the transferred/moved case), and the rule's own tie-breaker "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" points the same way, so (Patient sk_leave_1 sk_group_2) asserts a change the sentence does not state.

Term propagation copies the antecedent event's stated day-level terms and explicitly falls back to "If the antecedent's day is unknown, emit just the day-part" — the night this "that night" points at is the sundown lighting, which carries no Day/Year term (the passage attaches Day 80 / Year 1 to the approval clause alone), so importing them onto sk_tend_1 would assert a date the text never gives the tending.

gaps_confirmed: "for the first time" — an nth-occasion adverbial over occurrences of the event has no licensed carrier (Ordinal ranks an entity on a scale, not occasions of an event), so the qualifier is silently dropped
new_gaps: A passage-initial date frame ("On day 80 of Year 1, the Council approved …") has no propagation mechanism to later clauses: the instruction set attaches calendar terms clause by clause, so every undated event in the passage — and the anaphoric "that night" — loses the day anchor the narrative supplies

An in-world calendar ("day 80 of Year 1"): the structured (Day n) / (Year n) terms presume Gregorian day-of-month and calendar year, so a day-of-year count and a bare regnal year have no specified term and the seeded date-ordering rules would read them wrongly

Coordinated time adjuncts on one clause ("at midnight and at the third watch") — nothing states whether to replicate the whole event once per adjunct (as here) or stack two Time atoms on a single event; the Coordination section covers clauses, VPs and NPs only
adjudication.defect_summary: Statement 69 should be (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_group_2) — leaving threads on the lantern moves them without altering them, so the object-change test (and its default-to-Theme fallback) gives Theme; the rest of the leave bundle, including the Location oblique and the silken_thread group, stands as parsed.
adjudication.notes: Everything else checks out against the instruction set: the postural "stood beside" correctly mints no event and takes the entity-attached (Past (Beside …)), the wick gets no invented PartOf to the lantern, and "after sundown" as (TimeAtLeast sk_land_1 sundown) is the licensed day-part-constant bound. PartOf vs Possession for "the lantern of the Harbor Station" and the bare kind fillers half_shift / mist_light are genuine coin-flips the instruction set leaves open, not defects.
